summary: the cases of tests/run loopdev on i686, against a loop device that writes its file without syncing it, one that takes a file whose length is not whole sectors, and one that is not told that the stick under its file has gone

argv: ARCH=i686 sh tests/proofs/guest.sh make rach2 && ARCH=i686 sh tests/proofs/guest.sh copy ${WORK} rach2/kernel

faults.name: unsynced-write
faults.summary: a write through the device writes the file and returns without syncing it, so /proc/loop counts no sync

faults.name: odd-length
faults.summary: a refusal omitted: a file whose length is not whole sectors is attached

faults.name: gone-unnoticed
faults.summary: a pulled stick not noticed: the loop device over a file on it is not told that its device has gone

edits.find:
klog(KLOG_WARN, "loop", "loop%d: the device under its file has gone", i);
        loops[i].dev.flags |= BLOCK_GONE;
